questions.enonce_markdown: Differentiate between system software and application software. Name an example in each case. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**System software** is the set of programs that control and manage the computer hardware and provide the platform on which other programs run (it works *for the computer*). It includes the operating system, utility programs, device drivers and language translators. *Example:* the Windows operating system (or Linux).

**Application software** is a program written to let the user carry out a particular task of their own (it works *for the user*), and it needs the system software in order to run. *Example:* a word processor such as Microsoft Word (or a spreadsheet such as Excel).

| | System software | Application software |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Manages and runs the hardware | Does a specific job for the user |
| Runs | From start-up, in the background | When the user starts it |
| Example | Operating system (Windows, Linux) | Word processor (MS Word) |

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the following features of a word processor:

(i) Editing

(ii) Mail merging

(iii) Cropping

(iv) Formatting

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Editing.** Changing the content of an existing document: inserting, deleting, copying, cutting, pasting and moving text, finding and replacing words, correcting spelling, and undoing mistakes.

**(ii) Mail merging.** Combining a main document (for example a standard letter containing merge fields) with a data source (for example a list of names and addresses) so that a personalised copy of the letter is produced automatically for each person on the list.

**(iii) Cropping.** Cutting off the unwanted outer parts of a picture or image inserted in the document, by trimming its edges, so that only the wanted part remains visible.

**(iv) Formatting.** Changing the appearance of the text and of the page without changing its content: font type, size and colour, bold, italic, underline, alignment, line spacing, bullets and numbering, borders, margins and page layout.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Briefly describe the differences between Manual Information System and an Automated Information System. (4 marks)

(ii) Give two examples of Computerised Information Systems. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Manual and automated information systems (4 marks).**

| | Manual information system | Automated (computerised) information system |
|---|---|---|
| How it works | Data is collected, stored and processed by people using paper, files, registers and calculations by hand | Data is collected, stored and processed by computers and software |
| Speed | Slow | Very fast |
| Accuracy | More errors (tiredness, hand-copying) | Fewer errors (calculations and checks done by the program) |
| Storage and retrieval | Bulky paper files, records are slow to find and can be lost or damaged | Large amounts of data in a small space, records found in seconds, backups possible |
| Sharing and security | One copy in one place, easy to steal or destroy | Data can be shared over a network and protected by passwords; needs electricity and trained staff |

**(ii) Two examples of computerised information systems (2 marks).** Any two of: a school records / student management system, a bank (ATM or core banking) system, an airline ticket reservation system, a hospital patient records system, a library management system, a payroll system.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Name any four components of a Data Transmission System. (4 marks)

(ii) Briefly describe the role of any two of the components listed above. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Four components of a data transmission system (4 marks).**

1. The **sender** (source or transmitter).
2. The **receiver** (destination).
3. The **transmission medium** (channel), for example a cable, an optical fibre or radio waves.
4. The **message** (the data, text, sound or images being sent).
5. The **protocol** (the agreed set of rules for sending and receiving).

Any four of these are accepted (a modem or network interface card is also accepted as the device that converts the signals).

**(ii) Role of two of the components (2 marks).**

- **Sender:** it creates the message and puts it into a form (signals) that can be sent over the medium.
- **Transmission medium:** it is the path that carries the signals from the sender to the receiver.
- **Receiver:** it accepts the signals and converts them back into a message that the user can understand.
- **Protocol:** it sets the rules for the format, speed and error checking of the data so that sender and receiver understand each other.

(Two of the above are enough.)
